items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: Now the famous drummer Peter Erskine, who is unbelievable, and one of my heroes

ctx.x: Speaking of hi-hats, we’re going to veer off here, but there was a couple of moments last night where you literally were just playing your hi-hat and the snare and almost pretending to play the bass drum. And the power in that, I’m just sort of mystified by it sometimes. It’s hard to teach I think.

I know. When it comes down to the time of the music, that’s the pulse, and that’s the quarter note. A quarter note gets a beat for those of you who are watching this who don’t know anything about music. A quarter note is the beat [taps steadily]. There’s the beat right there. And those are quarter notes. One, two, three, four. So when you can master just playing quarter notes at a steady tempo and not waver no matter what’s going on around you, then I think you’ve really stumbled onto something. Maybe not…

stuff at the very beginning for about a minute. And then he stops and he goes like this. The quarter note’s on the hi-hat and that’s it. No opening and closing, just quarter notes. And he looks at the camera and he goes, “if you can’t do this for three minutes without wavering, then all the other stuff is just a bad imitation of good drummers.” And I thought that was beautiful. That was right up my alley. I’ve never met Peter. I’ve always loved everything he did. I saw him at Carnegie Hall in 1976 with Maynard.…
